name: Plasma Cell Tumor

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: International Myeloma Working Group Criteria for Plasmacytoma

criteria.description: Histological confirmation of monoclonal plasma cell infiltration in a localized tumor
Bone marrow plasma cells less than 10% without evidence of systemic multiple myeloma
Absence of additional bone lesions on skeletal survey or advanced imaging
Low or absent serum/urine monoclonal protein levels

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histological confirmation of localized monoclonal plasma cell tumor with bone marrow plasma cells <10% and no additional bone lesions on imaging
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Distinction from multiple myeloma is critical for diagnosis and management.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Localized soft tissue mass with monoclonal plasma cell infiltration
searchTerms: localized soft tissue tumor with plasma cells
soft tissue swelling with immune cell infiltration

pathognomonic.symptomName: Solitary bone lesion with plasma cell proliferation
searchTerms: single bone tumor with plasma cells

common.symptomName: Localized bone pain at tumor site
searchTerms: pain at tumor site in bone

common.symptomName: Swelling or palpable mass in affected area
searchTerms: swelling or lump in affected area

common.symptomName: Mild anemia related to marrow involvement
searchTerms: low red blood cells due to marrow involvement

common.symptomName: Mild monoclonal gammopathy detected in serum or urine
searchTerms: small monoclonal protein in blood or urine

occasional.symptomName: Neurological symptoms due to nerve compression

searchTerms: tiredness due to low blood count

rare.symptomName: Renal impairment due to light chain deposition
searchTerms: kidney damage from light chain deposits
renal impairment due to protein buildup

rare.symptomName: Systemic symptoms such as weight loss and fever
searchTerms: general symptoms like fatigue and fever

rare.symptomName: Extramedullary plasmacytoma involving upper respiratory tract
searchTerms: tumor in nose or throat area

laboratory: Monoclonal protein (M-protein) spike in serum or urine electrophoresis
Bone marrow biopsy showing <10% plasma cells
imaging: Solitary lytic bone lesion on skeletal survey or MRI
Absence of multiple bone lesions on PET-CT or whole-body MRI
genetic: Clonal plasma cell population with immunoglobulin light chain restriction
other: Histopathological confirmation of monoclonal plasma cell tumor
Immunohistochemistry positive for CD138 and monoclonal light chain

distinguishingFeatures: Multiple bone lesions rather than solitary
More pronounced systemic symptoms and organ damage

redFlags: Rapidly enlarging mass with bone destruction
Neurological deficits indicating spinal cord or nerve compression
Signs of systemic multiple myeloma such as hypercalcemia, anemia, or renal failure
references: International Myeloma Working Group. Criteria for the diagnosis of plasmacytoma. Leukemia. 2021.
Kyle RA, Rajkumar SV. Plasma cell disorders. Lancet. 2004.
